source.title: Some of My Favorite Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit ball in R3 and let λ1 = π2 be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of −Δ on Ω. For the boundary value problem −Δu = u5 + λu in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, and for parameters 0 < λ ≤ λ1/4, does there exist a nontrivial smooth solution u that is not identically zero?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1.1 (implicit in ([BrNi1]). Assume that (1.2) 0 < λ ≤ λ1/4. Does there exist a solution u 6≡ 0 of (1.1)?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit disc in R2 and consider the Ginzburg–Landau Dirichlet problem −Δu = ε−2 u(1 − |u|2) in Ω with boundary condition u(x) = x on ∂Ω. If Uε(x) = (x/|x|) fε(|x|) is the standard radial solution coming from the associated ODE for fε, is Uε the only solution of this boundary value problem for a given ε > 0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.1 ([BBH, Problem 10 in Chapter XI]). Is the radial solution Uε the only solution of (2.1)?

accepted.question_text: For the same unit-disc Ginzburg–Landau problem with boundary condition u(x) = x on ∂Ω, let Eε(u) = (1/2)∫Ω |∇u|2 + (1/(4ε2))∫Ω (|u|2 − 1)2 over H1_g(Ω; R2). Is the radial solution Uε a global minimizer of Eε on H1_g(Ω; R2) for every ε > 0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.2. Is Uε a minimizer of Eε on H1_g(Ω; R2) for any ε > 0?

accepted.question_text: Fix p > 2. On the unit disc Ω ⊂ R2 with boundary data g(x) = x on ∂Ω, consider the p-Ginzburg–Landau energy Eε,p(u) = (1/p)∫Ω |∇u|p + (1/(4ε2))∫Ω (|u|2 − 1)2 on W1,p_g(Ω; R2). If uε is any minimizer, or more generally any critical point, of Eε,p, does uε(x) converge to x/|x| on Ω \ {0} as ε → 0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.3 ([BM, Open Problem 30]). Assume p > 2 and let uε be any minimizer (resp. critical point) of Eε,p on W1,p_g(Ω, R2). Does uε(x) → x/|x| in Ω \ {0} as ε → 0?

accepted.question_text: Consider entire smooth solutions u: R2 → R2 of −Δu = u(1 − |u|2) such that |u(x)| → 1 as |x| → ∞. Writing q = deg(u, ∞), must every such solution be, up to translation and multiplication by a complex number of modulus 1, the standard degree-q vortex Vq determined by the radial profile gq? In other words, must u(x) = αVq(x − x0) for some |α| = 1 and x0 ∈ R2?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.4 ([BBH, Problem 14], [BMR], [Br3]). Let u be any solution of (2.5) - (2.6). Does u coincide with Vq modulo rotation and translation, where q = deg(u, ∞)? I.e., is u(x) = αVq(x − x0) for some α ∈ C, |α| = 1, and x0 ∈ R2?

accepted.question_text: If u: R2 → R2 is a smooth solution of −Δu = u(1 − |u|2) and satisfies |u(x)| → 1 as |x| → ∞, must the potential-energy integral ∫R2 (|u|2 − 1)2 be finite?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.5 ([BMR, Problem 2], [Br3, Open Problem 2]). Assume that u satisfies (2.5) and (2.6). Does (2.11) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit disc in R2, let 0 < R < 1, and prescribe boundary data g(x, y) = (Rx, Ry, √(1 − R2)) on ∂Ω. For harmonic maps u: Ω → S2 solving −Δui = ui|∇u|2 with u = g on ∂Ω, two explicit solutions u and ū are known. Are there any other solutions besides these two explicit ones?
accepted.context_brief: harmonic maps from disc to sphere

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.1 ([BrCo]). Assume g is given by (3.6). Are there other solutions of (3.1)-(3.3) besides u and ū?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω = B3 be the unit ball in R3, let g: ∂Ω ≅ S2 → S2 be smooth with degree zero, and consider harmonic maps u ∈ H1_g(Ω; S2) solving −Δui = ui|∇u|2 in Ω with u = g on ∂Ω. Does there always exist at least one harmonic map satisfying these equations that is continuous on the closed ball?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.1 ([HaLi], [Ha], [Br5, Open Problem 3]). Assume that (4.6) holds. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying (4.1)-(4.3)?

accepted.question_text: Under the same degree-zero boundary condition g: ∂B3 → S2, consider the constrained minimization problem inf{E(u): u ∈ H1_g(B3; S2) ∩ C(B3̄)}, where E(u) = ∫B3 |∇u|2. Is this infimum attained by some continuous map u on the closed ball?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.2 ([HaLi], [Ha]). Is the (4.8) Inf {E(u); u ∈ H1_g(Ω; S2) ∩ C(Ω)̄} achieved?

accepted.question_text: Let R(u) be the relaxed energy on H1_g(B3; S2) associated with approximation by continuous maps under weak H1 convergence. Are minimizers of the relaxed-energy problem min{R(u): u ∈ H1_g(B3; S2)} continuous on the closed ball? At a minimum, is at least one minimizer continuous?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.3 ([BBC]). Are the minimizers of (4.10) continuous on Ω? (Is it true for at least one of the minimizers?)

accepted.question_text: Let u be a minimizer of the relaxed-energy problem min{R(u): u ∈ H1_g(B3; S2)}. Must the singular interaction term S(u) vanish? Equivalently, must the distributional Jacobian Ju be zero, or equivalently must u admit strong H1 approximation by continuous maps in H1_g(B3; S2) ∩ C(B3̄)?
accepted.context_brief: vanishing singular part of relaxed minimizer

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.4. Let u be a minimizer of (4.10). Is it true that S(u) = 0, i.e., Ju = 0 ? or equivalently that there exists a sequence (un) in H1_g(Ω; S2) ∩ C(Ω)̄ such that un converges to u strongly in H1?

accepted.question_text: For 1 < p ≤ 2, does there exist a universal constant c such that every map f ∈ W1/p,p(S1; S1) satisfies |deg f| ≤ c(p − 1) ∬S1×S1 |f(x) − f(y)|p / |x − y|2 dx dy?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.1 ([Br7, Remark 7]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that, for every 1 < p ≤ 2, (5.6) | deg f| ≤ c(p − 1) ∫∫ |f(x) − f(y)|^p / |x − y|^2 ∀f ∈ W1/p,p(S1; S1)?

accepted.question_text: For the sharp topological-degree estimate |deg f| ≤ C ∬S1×S1 1{|f(x)−f(y)|≥√3} / |x−y|2 dx dy on continuous circle-valued maps, is there a simpler and more geometric proof? What is the best possible constant C in this inequality, and is that best constant attained by some map?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.2 ([BM, Open Problem 18]). Is there a simpler, more geometric proof of Theorem 5.2? What is the best constant C in (5.9)? Is it achieved?

accepted.question_text: Given Iδ(f) = ∬S1×S1 1{|f(x)−f(y)|≥δ} / |x−y|2 dx dy for a continuous map f: S1 → S1, does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f| ≤ c δ Iδ(f) for every f and every δ ≤ √3?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.3 ([Br7, Open Problem 3]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that (5.12) | deg f| ≤ cδIδ(f) ∀f ∈ C(S1; S1) ∀δ ≤ √3?

accepted.question_text: For 1 < p < ∞ and integer degree d, let mp,d be the infimum of the W1/p,p-energy over all circle-valued maps f on S1 with deg f = d. Is mp,d always equal to |d| mp,1? Is the infimum defining mp,d always attained? If exact linearity fails, is there an explicit formula for lim d→+∞ mp,d / d = inf d>0 mp,d / d?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.4 ([BM, Open Problems 22 and 23]). Let 1 < p < ∞. Is true that (5.15) mp,d = |d|mp,1 ∀d ∈ Z? Is the inf in (5.13) achieved? Assuming that (5.15) does not hold, is there an explicit formula for (5.16) lim d→+∞ mp,d / d = inf d>0 mp,d / d?

accepted.question_text: Suppose f and g are circle-valued maps on S1 with identical Fourier modulus data, meaning |an(f)| = |an(g)| for every integer n. When f and g lie in weaker regularity classes than W1/3,3—specifically in W1/p,p with p > 3, or in Hölder class C0,α with α ≤ 1/3—must one still have deg f = deg g? The question remains open even under mixed stronger assumptions where one map is above and the other below the known threshold.
accepted.context_brief: hearing the degree below known threshold

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.5. What happens to Theorem 5.5 when f, g ∈ W1/p,p(S1; S1) with p > 3 (resp. f, g ∈ C0,α(S1: S1) with α ≤ 1/3)? The problem is open even under the stronger assumption that f ∈ W1/p,p with 2 < p ≤ 3 and g ∈ W1/q,q with q > 3 (resp. f ∈ C0,α with α > 1/3 and g ∈ C0,β with β ≤ 1/3).

accepted.question_text: For either a fixed exponent p > 3 or a fixed Hölder exponent α ≤ 1/3, does there exist a summation process (σn,ε), depending only on p or only on α, such that for every map f in W1/p,p(S1; S1) or respectively in C0,α(S1; S1), the limit lim ε→0 Σn∈Z n|an(f)|2 σn,ε recovers deg f?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.6. Given any p > 3 (resp. α ≤ 1/3) does there exist a summation process (σn,ε), depending only on p (resp. α) such that (5.25) holds for every f ∈ W1/p,p (resp. f ∈ C0,α)?

accepted.question_text: For every continuous map f: S1 → S1, or more generally every VMO map f: S1 → S1, is there some summation process (σn,ε) that may depend on f itself and for which lim ε→0 Σn∈Z n|an(f)|2 σn,ε equals deg f?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.7. Given any f ∈ C(S1; S1) (resp. f ∈ V MO(S1; S1)) does there exist a summation process (σn,ε) (depending on f) such that (5.25) holds?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a continuous circle-valued map f on S1, or even a VMO circle-valued map, for which no summation process whatsoever can recover the degree from the Fourier-modulus expression Σn∈Z n|an(f)|2 σn,ε in the limit ε → 0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.8. Does there exist some f ∈ C(S1; S1) (resp. f ∈ V MO(S1; S1)) such that for any summation process (σn,ε), Σn∈Z n|an(f)|2σn,ε does not converge to deg f?

accepted.question_text: Let Ed denote the homotopy class of maps in H1(S2; S2) of degree d, and define DistH1(Ed1, Ed2) = sup f∈Ed1 inf g∈Ed2 ||∇(f − g)||L2. Is it true for all integers d1 and d2 that DistH1(Ed1, Ed2)2 = 8π |d1 − d2|?
accepted.context_brief: distance between H1 homotopy classes on S2

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.9 ([BMS]). Is true that (5.28) Dist2_H1 (Ed1, Ed2) = 8π|d1 − d2| ∀d1, d2 ∈ Z?

accepted.question_text: Let B be the closed unit ball in RN and let f: B → B be a VMO map. Must it be true that for every ε > 0, the approximate fixed-point set {x ∈ B : |f(x) − x| < ε} has positive measure?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.10. Let B be the closed unit ball in RN and let f be a VMO map from B into itself. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the set {x ∈ B; |f(x) − x| < ε} has positive measure?

accepted.question_text: Consider the extremal solution u* for −Δu = λf(u) in a smooth bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ RN with u = 0 on ∂Ω, in dimension N ≥ 10. First take f(u) = eu. Must u* be unbounded? If some convex domains yield a bounded extremal solution for eu, can one instead find another nonlinearity f satisfying the standard assumptions f(0) > 0, f increasing and convex, and f(t)/t → ∞, possibly depending on Ω, for which the corresponding extremal solution is unbounded?
accepted.context_brief: unbounded extremal solutions in high dimension

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.1 ([BrVa], [Br6]). Assume Ω is a bounded smooth convex set in RN, N ≥ 10. Let f(u) = eu. Is u∗ unbounded? If the answer is negative for some domains Ω, can one find other functions f satisfying (6.2)-(6.3) (possibly depending on Ω) such that u∗ ∈/ L∞(Ω)?

accepted.question_text: Assume the extremal solution u* of the semilinear Dirichlet problem −Δu = λf(u) is unbounded. What structure can its blow-up set have? In particular, when the domain Ω is convex, must the blow-up set consist of a single point?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.2 ([BrVa], [Br6]). Assume u∗ ∈/ L∞(Ω). What can be said about the blow-up set of u∗? Does it consist of a single point when Ω is convex?

accepted.question_text: Does the estimate ||ψ − ∫ψ||H1/2+W1,1 ≤ C ||∇ψ||H−1/2+L1 hold for all appropriate test functions ψ, where the left side is measured in the sum space H1/2 + W1,1 and the right side in H−1/2 + L1?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7.1 ([BoBr]). Does (7.9) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let U be the unique minimizer in BV(Ω) ∩ L2(Ω) of the Rudin–Osher–Fatemi type functional Φ(u) = ∫Ω |∇u| + (1/2)∫Ω |u − f|2 on a smooth bounded domain Ω ⊂ RN, with smooth datum f. Must the distributional gradient ∇U belong to BV(Ω)?
accepted.context_brief: BV regularity of TV minimizer gradient

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8.1 ([Br10, Open Problem 1]). Does ∇U belong to BV (Ω)?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a smooth bounded connected domain in RN, let p ≥ 1, and for a measurable function u define Φλ,p(u) as the measure of pairs (x, y) ∈ Ω × Ω for which |u(x) − u(y)|p / |x − y|p+N ≥ λ. If lim inf λ→∞ λ Φλ,p(u) = 0, must u be constant almost everywhere?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.1 ([BVY, Open Problem 1]). Assume that u satisfies (9.4) lim inf λ→∞ λΦλ,p(u) = 0 for some p ≥ 1. Can one conclude that u is a constant?

accepted.question_text: For 1 < p < ∞, does there exist a constant C depending only on p, N, and Ω such that every measurable u satisfies ||∇u||Lp^p ≤ C lim inf λ→∞ λ Φλ,p(u), with the convention that ||∇u||Lp = ∞ when u is not in W1,p(Ω)? Likewise for p = 1, does there exist C depending on N and Ω such that ||∇u||M ≤ C lim inf λ→∞ λ Φλ,1(u), where ||∇u||M is the total variation measure and is taken to be ∞ outside BV(Ω)?
accepted.context_brief: liminf control of Sobolev or BV norm

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.2 ([BSVY, Section 7.2]). Given any 1 < p < ∞, is there a constant C = C(p, N, Ω) such that, for all measurable functions u, (9.5) ||∇u||^p_Lp ≤ C lim inf λ→∞ λΦλ,p(u)? ... Similarly for p = 1, is there a constant C = C(N, Ω) such that, for all measurable functions u, (9.6) ||∇u||M ≤ C lim inf λ→∞ λΦλ,1(u)?

accepted.question_text: As λ → ∞, do the functionals λ Φλ,p Γ-converge to the Sobolev or BV seminorm functional Ψ, namely Ψ(u) = cp ||∇u||Lp^p on W1,p(Ω) and +∞ outside W1,p(Ω) when p > 1, and Ψ(u) = c1 ||∇u||M on BV(Ω) and +∞ outside BV(Ω) when p = 1, for some positive constants cp and c1?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.3 ([BSVY, Section 7.3]). Does the family of functionals λΦλ,p converge as λ → ∞, in the sense of Γ-convergence, to the functional Ψ ... for some positive constants cp and c1 ?

accepted.question_text: Let Q be the unit cube in RN, N ≥ 3, and let fN(t) be the sharp relative isoperimetric profile inf{P(S): S ⊂ Q measurable and |S| = t}, where P(S) is the relative perimeter inside Q. Is there an explicit formula for fN analogous to the known two-dimensional formula? In particular, is fN(t) identically equal to 1 for t near 1/2?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10.1 ([BreBru]). Is there a formula similar to (10.2) for fN (t) when N ≥ 3? In particular, is it true that fN (t) ≡ 1 near t = 1/2?

Extracted five explicit Ginzburg–Landau open problems from Section 2.
Extracted the explicit harmonic-map multiplicity problem from Section 3.
Extracted four explicit open problems on continuous harmonic maps and relaxed energy from Section 4.
Extracted ten explicit open problems on degree theory, Fourier data, summation processes, and homotopy-class distance from Section 5.
Extracted two explicit open problems on extremal solutions from Section 6.
Extracted the Bourgain–Brezis estimate question from Section 7.
Extracted the BV regularity question for the total-variation minimizer from Section 8.
Extracted three explicit open problems on λΦλ,p from Section 9.
Extracted the explicit relative-isoperimetric problem from Section 10.

Rewrote each accepted item into a standalone question by expanding notation such as Ω, λ1, Uε, Eε, Eε,p, Vq, R(u), S(u), Ju, mp,d, Φλ,p, and fN only where the source text supplied the needed definitions.
No near-duplicate explicit open problems required merging; one canonical question was kept for each labeled open problem.
